notes: Late rate was 19.0% against a 5.8% baseline (delta 13.2 points), with 1,328 late orders out of 7,003 delivered.
The top driver was carrier_transit: transit averaged 12.97 days versus a 9.06-day baseline, roughly 3.9 days longer, while handling was only slightly above baseline (3.33 vs 3.19 days).
The problem was systemic: excluding the two worst states still left a 23.7% late rate, and late orders spanned 466 sellers with the top 5 accounting for only 11.5% of them.
It was concentrated geographically: RJ ran 34.5% late (baseline 10.5%, 208 excess late orders), MG 20.4% (baseline 3.3%, 147 excess), and SP 9.4% (baseline 4.1%, 158 excess).
Late deliveries coincided with much worse reviews: average 2.07 versus 4.21 for on-time, with a 59.3% one-star share versus 7.9%.

definitions: Baseline: all other months of January 2017 to August 2018, same filters

caveats: The data shows where delay occurred, not why (observational data).
Order-level lateness is attributed to every seller in a multi-seller order.
Some category samples are small, e.g. audio with only 33 orders, so its 42.4% rate is unstable.
Promised days were actually shorter than baseline (22.03 vs 23.78), so the elevated late rate is not explained by longer promises.

evidence.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FILTER(WHERE purchase_month = CAST('2018-03-01' AS DATE)) AS n_period, COUNT(*) FILTER(WHERE purchase_month = CAST('2018-03-01' AS DATE) AND is_late) AS late_period, COUNT(*) FILTER(WHERE purchase_month <> CAST('2018-03-01' AS DATE)) AS n_base, COUNT(*) FILTER(WHERE purchase_month <> CAST('2018-03-01' AS DATE) AND is_late) AS late_base FROM orders WHERE is_delivered AND purchase_month >= CAST('2017-01-01' AS DATE) AND purchase_month < CAST('2018-09-01' AS DATE) AND (CAST(NULL AS TEXT) IS NULL OR customer_state = NULL) LIMIT 501

SELECT purchase_month = CAST('2018-03-01' AS DATE) AS in_period, ROUND(CAST(AVG(seller_handling_days) AS DECIMAL), 2) AS handling_days, ROUND(CAST(AVG(carrier_transit_days) AS DECIMAL), 2) AS transit_days, ROUND(CAST(AVG(promised_days) AS DECIMAL), 2) AS promised_days, COUNT(*) AS n FROM orders WHERE is_delivered AND purchase_month >= CAST('2017-01-01' AS DATE) AND purchase_month < CAST('2018-09-01' AS DATE) AND (CAST(NULL AS TEXT) IS NULL OR customer_state = NULL) GROUP BY 1 LIMIT 501

SELECT customer_state AS state, COUNT(*) FILTER(WHERE purchase_month = CAST('2018-03-01' AS DATE)) AS n_period, COUNT(*) FILTER(WHERE purchase_month = CAST('2018-03-01' AS DATE) AND is_late) AS late_period, COUNT(*) FILTER(WHERE purchase_month <> CAST('2018-03-01' AS DATE)) AS n_base, COUNT(*) FILTER(WHERE purchase_month <> CAST('2018-03-01' AS DATE) AND is_late) AS late_base FROM orders WHERE is_delivered AND purchase_month >= CAST('2017-01-01' AS DATE) AND purchase_month < CAST('2018-09-01' AS DATE) GROUP BY customer_state ORDER BY customer_state LIMIT 501

SELECT category, COUNT(DISTINCT order_id) FILTER(WHERE purchase_month = CAST('2018-03-01' AS DATE)) AS n_period, COUNT(DISTINCT order_id) FILTER(WHERE purchase_month = CAST('2018-03-01' AS DATE) AND is_late) AS late_period, COUNT(DISTINCT order_id) FILTER(WHERE purchase_month <> CAST('2018-03-01' AS DATE)) AS n_base, COUNT(DISTINCT order_id) FILTER(WHERE purchase_month <> CAST('2018-03-01' AS DATE) AND is_late) AS late_base FROM order_items WHERE is_late IS NOT NULL AND purchase_month >= CAST('2017-01-01' AS DATE) AND purchase_month < CAST('2018-09-01' AS DATE) AND (CAST(NULL AS TEXT) IS NULL OR customer_state = NULL) GROUP BY category HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT order_id) FILTER(WHERE purchase_month = CAST('2018-03-01' AS DATE)) >= 30 ORDER BY category LIMIT 501

WITH s AS (SELECT seller_id, COUNT(DISTINCT order_id) AS late_orders FROM order_items WHERE is_late AND purchase_month = CAST('2018-03-01' AS DATE) AND (CAST(NULL AS TEXT) IS NULL OR customer_state = NULL) GROUP BY seller_id) SELECT COUNT(*) AS sellers_with_late_orders, (SELECT SUM(late_orders) FROM (SELECT late_orders FROM s ORDER BY late_orders DESC LIMIT 5) AS t) AS top5_late_orders FROM s LIMIT 501

SELECT seller_id, COUNT(DISTINCT order_id) FILTER(WHERE purchase_month = CAST('2018-03-01' AS DATE)) AS n_period, COUNT(DISTINCT order_id) FILTER(WHERE purchase_month = CAST('2018-03-01' AS DATE) AND is_late) AS late_period, COUNT(DISTINCT order_id) FILTER(WHERE purchase_month <> CAST('2018-03-01' AS DATE)) AS n_base, COUNT(DISTINCT order_id) FILTER(WHERE purchase_month <> CAST('2018-03-01' AS DATE) AND is_late) AS late_base FROM order_items WHERE is_late IS NOT NULL AND purchase_month >= CAST('2017-01-01' AS DATE) AND purchase_month < CAST('2018-09-01' AS DATE) AND (CAST(NULL AS TEXT) IS NULL OR customer_state = NULL) GROUP BY seller_id HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT order_id) FILTER(WHERE purchase_month = CAST('2018-03-01' AS DATE)) >= 30 ORDER BY seller_id LIMIT 501

SELECT is_late, COUNT(review_score) AS n_reviews, ROUND(CAST(AVG(review_score) AS DECIMAL), 2) AS avg_score, COUNT(*) FILTER(WHERE review_score = 1) AS one_star FROM orders WHERE is_delivered AND purchase_month = CAST('2018-03-01' AS DATE) AND (CAST(NULL AS TEXT) IS NULL OR customer_state = NULL) GROUP BY is_late ORDER BY is_late LIMIT 501

headline: March 2018 was genuinely elevated for late deliveries: 19.0% of the 7,003 delivered orders were late versus a 5.8% baseline, a gap of 13.2 percentage points, and the pattern was systemic rather than confined to a few states or sellers.
